Patrick Stewart 's final film is set to be  Avengers: Doomsday ,  where he reprises his role as Professor Charles Xavier one last time.

To honor the actor, Marvel's Kevin Feige revealed they are planning to add a special tribute to the film, set for release on December 18.

"We’re long done filming that movie, and he did an amazing job for us," the studio head told Entertainment Weekly . "We’re looking now at how we can put something together that honors and respects our friend."

Stewart died on October 28  from Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia and was originally offered the chance to appear in both Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars , which will be released at the end of 2027. articles.title: Twilight Fans Have Been Talking About That James Bond Scene. There’s Even More To It Than We Thought
articles.summary: Before he was 007, he was Cullen. Edward Cullen.
articles.content:
When it was announced that Robert Pattinson had been cast as James Bond , Twilight fans everywhere did a little cheer. Especially if you were Team Edward ! What a good long-term investment that’s turned out to be! However, the most popular Twilight -related reaction to Pattinson being 007 stems from the fact that the iconic spy was brought up in the vampire movie. As it turns out, there’s a whole new layer to that scene we didn’t know about.

Isn’t that wild? James Bond is literally said in Twilight right before the current James Bond appears. However, there’s more to it. The movie’s director, Catherine Hardwicke, revealed something new about the scene while talking about the casting on The Kyle Buchanan Show . In her words:

That happened 18 years before it became a reality. I guess it goes to show the role has been right for Robert Pattinson all along given those on the set of Twilight were thinking about it, too. Pattinson didn’t earn the role easily, either. All sorts of other eligible actors such as Nicholas Hoult, Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and Jack Lowden reportedly auditioned for Denis Villeneuve’s film. Charlie Cox also recently said he was shot down for being “too old” even though he’s just three years older than Pattinson.

While it’s perhaps a bit surprising Amazon MGM Studios didn’t opt for an actor who was an unknown , Jeff Bezos has said that in the screen tests it was “so obvious” Pattinson was their Bond that they didn’t dare pick anyone else. We can’t wait to see what his Bond will be like, and given his career thus far, it sounds like it might be unexpected.

articles.title: Oscars Visual Effects Top 20 Revealed: Disney Leads With Four Titles as ‘The Odyssey,’ ‘Ramayana,’ ‘Dune: Part Three’ and ‘Wildwood’ Make the Cut (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: The Oscar race for visual effects is down to 20, and the road to the 99th Academy Awards runs through Ithaca, Motunui and a galaxy far, far away. The Academy’s Visual Effects Branch notified the artisans behind the 20 films advancing to the next round ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. Through multiple sources, Variety has […]
articles.content:
The Oscar race for visual effects is down to 20, and the road to the 99th Academy Awards runs through Ithaca, Motunui and a galaxy far, far away.

The Academy’s Visual Effects Branch notified the artisans behind the 20 films advancing to the next round ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. Through multiple sources, Variety has confirmed 19 of the finalists, including Denis Villeneuve’s “Dune: Part Three,” Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” Phil Lord and Christopher Miller’s “Project Hail Mary,” Steven Spielberg’s “Disclosure Day” and Marvel Studios’ “ Avengers: Doomsday ” from Anthony and Joe Russo. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'One & Only’ Campaign: BOTOX® Cosmetic (onabotulinumtoxinA) Has Been FDA Approved for Over 20 Years Andrew Scott on Starring in ‘Elsinore’ and Feeling ‘Very Grateful’ to Be an Out Gay Actor

The Academy does not release the top 20 externally and declines to comment or confirm which films advanced.

Disney leads the confirmed titles with four. Alongside “Avengers: Doomsday,” the studio lands Jon Favreau’s “Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu,” 20th Century Studios’ “Whalefall” and Thomas Kail’s live-action “Moana,” which brings Dwayne Johnson back as the demigod Maui.

Skydance (formerly Warner Bros Discovery) took three of the spots: “Dune: Part Three,” Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s Tom Cruise-led “Digger” and Craig Gillespie’s “Supergirl” from former DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran. But the studio also sees four contenders fall short.

Villeneuve’s stakes are historic. Both “Dune” and “Dune: Part Two” won the visual effects Oscar, and in March, “Avatar: Fire and Ash” made James Cameron’s franchise three-for-three in the category. “Dune: Part Three,” which opens Dec. 18, now puts Villeneuve two steps from the same trilogy sweep. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Universal Pictures booked both of its summer event films, “The Odyssey” and “Disclosure Day,” while Amazon MGM Studios goes two-for-two with “Project Hail Mary” and Kyle Balda’s “The Sheep Detectives.”

Nolan’s track record in the category is just as formidable. “Inception,” “Interstellar” and “Tenet” each won the visual effects Oscar. However, the branch famously left “Oppenheimer” off its top 20 for the 96th Academy Awards. Spielberg has been here before, too, with “Jurassic Park,” which won the category in 1994.

Two of the more intriguing finalists come from outside the Hollywood studio system. Takashi Yamazaki’s “ Godzilla Minus Zero ” follows “Godzilla Minus One,” which won the category at the 96th Oscars and delivered the franchise its first Academy Award. Laika’s stop-motion “Wildwood,” directed by Travis Knight, gives the studio a chance to return to a category it cracked with Knight’s “Kubo and the Two Strings,” one of only two animated films ever nominated for visual effects, along with “The Nightmare Before Christmas.”

Sony lands three big movies in the field. Leading the charge is Destin Daniel Cretton’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and the still-to-be-released “Jumanji: Open World” advancing alongside “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend,” the Indian mythological epic. “Ramayana” follows S.S. Rajamoulili’s “RRR,” which reached the top 20 for the 95th Oscars and signals the branch’s continued appetite for large-scale spectacle from outside Hollywood.

A24 also lands a spot with “Backrooms,” the feature directorial debut of 21-year-old Kane Parsons, whose YouTube series turned the internet’s liminal-space legend into a box office phenomenon, grossing more than $400 million worldwide.

Paramount received a split verdict. David Ayer’s survival thriller “Heart of the Beast,” starring Brad Pitt, advanced, but Variety confirmed that two of the studio’s other contenders, “Ebenezer” with Johnny Depp and the video game adaptation “Street Fighter,” did not make the top 20.

Netflix also breaks through with Peter Berg’s epic war drama “The Mosquito Bowl,” one year after the streamer placed “Frankenstein” and “The Electric State” on the shortlist. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

That leaves one spot unconfirmed, with a few titles still awaiting confirmation. Variety will update this story as additional finalists are confirmed.

The preliminary voting period for the Oscars shortlist begins Monday, Dec. 7, at 9 a.m. PT and ends Friday, Dec. 11, at 5 p.m. PT. The shortlists in all categories will be announced Tuesday, Dec. 15. Afterward, the VFX bake-offs will take place during the Academy’s Jan. 8-10 voting events, when the 10 shortlisted films will be presented to branch members for final nomination consideration. Nominations voting runs Jan. 11-15, with the nominations announced Thursday, Jan. 21.

The 99th Academy Awards will be held Sunday, March 14, at the Dolby Theatre at Ovation Hollywood and will air live on ABC.

articles.title: 'Dancing With the Stars' Finalist Connor Wood Has Already Won: "I Feel Really Good"
articles.summary: The 31-year-old comedian has made it to the finale of the dance competition series show, even though he never quite expected it: "I really can't put my finger on why this clicked for me, but I leaned in a lot."
articles.content:
Comedian and podcaster Connor Wood has become a bit of a fan favorite on this season of Dancing With the Stars . "If we're not in practice, I feel like I'm missing practice," the 31-year-old tells The Hollywood Reporter on a Zoom call. It's a rare rainy day in Los Angeles, and the season 35 contestant is finding a second to rest amidst crazy rehearsal schedules.

He and partner Rylee Arnold have taken each challenge in stride. The pair have found themselves amongst the five couples advancing to the show's finale , airing Tuesday night. Wood's viral social media moments have certainly helped endear viewers, however, his steadily improving dancing skills don't hurt. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV 'Dancing With the Stars' Season 35 Couples Perform Their Last Dances as a Winner Is Crowned in the Finale: See the Scores, Who Won (Updating Live) TV Where to Stream 'Dancing With the Stars' Season 35 Finale Live Online

"I have been really intentional about my life and making sure I don't ever work really hard," he says, cheekily. "This has changed that completely, flipped it on its head."

Heading into the final episode, he and the dancers are working with six hours a day of rehearsal to get themselves in prime condition. "Every minute of that is necessary for the show," he notes.

Below, Wood speaks with THR about heading into the DWTS finale, the reaction to his viral Jennifer Lawrence moment and dealing with the online hate.

How do you feel going into the finals?

I feel really good. Me and Rylee, we went into the semifinals, and that was the hard part. It was two brand new dances, two long dances, two very fast hard dances, and this one is fun. We're going out there, we're putting on a show. It really is for us, which is fun. It's for the fans, [but] it's [also] for us. It's something that hasn't been seen before. We're doing a really cool dichotomy of dances too. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

What days are the longest for you?

The day after the show, we film basically what you see before we dance. We do all of the face-to-face interviews. We do the one-on-one interview, and then we do the group session interview. This is obviously a bigger one. There's three dances, so they have three videos that they had to make. There's one for each dance, and then they'll film rehearsal and stuff for the filler. But I also have the podcast that I do, so that was 9 a.m. to 12 p.m., and then we filmed from 12 p.m to 10 p.m.

It was long, but it's all needed. That's the thing. Sometimes you go onto a set or something, and it's like we're doing a take for the 15th time, and I'm like, "I promise you I'm getting worse. Every time we do another one, I promise you're getting a worse take from me." This is not the case. This one you do get better as you put more hours in, which is an annoying, frustrating thing that that is true. The harder you work, the better you get.

What were you expecting for yourself coming in versus where you are now?

I wasn't expecting anything for myself, honestly. I've only ever danced at weddings. I have no pride when it comes to sticking with something. I'm happy to throw in the towel. You'll quit while you're ahead. I'll quit while I'm behind. I don't think there's any shame in that. I am competitive though, which is weird. We had to stop playing Monopoly in my family home because I took it too seriously. But that wasn't part of this — I really can't put my finger on why this clicked for me, but I leaned in a lot. I've done some really TikTok cringe things that I wouldn't normally have done. It's been so well received, it's a vulnerability thing, I guess, that's been nice to be a part of. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

How do you get through these red carpets to make it an actually enjoyable experience?

That's my bread and butter. Hamming it up on the carpet with interviews, that is my Dancing With The Stars . A funny thing that I've realized is that obviously I'm not the best dancer on the show or even freaking close. I'm aware of that. I feel like people don't realize that. I don't think I'm Zeus on the dance floor. I'm very aware of what I'm capable of, but people also aren't seeing that dance is a part of the whole of this show, and doing press and meeting fans and doing X, Y, Z, it all makes up that whole. Anytime we spend these 12, 15 hour days creating packages and personifying these people that are on TV, it helps the case. If they see that you're working really hard, if they see that you're having fun in the press lines. If you're being vulnerable, and you're oversharing, people really like that, they relate to it. That's what that is. I look forward to doing interviews because that's where I feel like I hit my stride on the dance floor is after the dance, and I can talk about how hard it was to learn in Argentine Tango.

Do you feel more confident in dancing now?

Yes, and I that's a natural progression with this whole thing. I'm learning the dances faster because I've been learning dance for three months. There's a baseline or a foundation that I'm pulling from. When Rylee gives me "Start here" and "do this," I know what she's talking about. I realized recently I'm personifying each dance. When a dance was really hard, I began to resent the dance on day two of rehearsal because I'm like, "We are not getting along, me and the samba, we're not getting along. I don't get the samba. It doesn't make sense to me." Getting past those couple weeks — I hit my stride in probably week six in this competition because I was not resenting the dance. It became easier for me to learn the dances. We saw my dancing. It's not the best, but I am having a lot more fun because I'm enjoying the process way more. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

With the show and being online, do you feel a bit of an overload? I'm sure you're not looking forward to hearing "8th Avenue" or "smoothie" said to you ever again. ( Laughs ).

I like when everybody's on board with something. What a harmless thing for everyone to be having fun with. That's good, clean, fun. It's easy. I know a lot of marketing coordinators probably had a really great weekly meeting when they turned in their social media reports and they had a video with a million views on their page for brand X, Y, Z, football team X, Y, Z. Everyone had so much fun. Everyone got to put a spin on that. That fired me up.

The rest of the internet, totally different story right now. We've gotten to a point where I have become a bit of a villain for some people.

Why do you think they feel that way?

I think that they think that I personally voted their favorite off, and it's like — I'm aware of my level of dance skill. I have nothing to do with me staying here. That's just been just the dark side of making it as far as we made it. My understanding is that the more that people go home, the more the fans of those people will go to someone else's page and villainize those people. That's sad, and it's just a testament to how invested people are in this show. A cool part of this show is that the fans are so invested. Like I said, the 8th Avenue thing, it's fun for people to be a part of things. Being on the other side of that is not as fun. It's part of the game. I signed up for it. I've never experienced that. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

It has to be tough given social media is a huge part of your job. You can't disengage as much.

Yeah. As we've gone through the season… First of all, I'm like, "Well, not getting on Twitter the rest of the season. That's a really interesting group of people." You want to get home from the 15-hour day, and you want to lay on your couch, your Lola blanket swaddling you like a newborn. Turn off your brain, look at your phone. The first thing on your phone is, "Connor Wood's still here? Who's he paying at ABC?" OK, scroll to the next thing. But that is part of it. This is weird and sick in the head, [but] I am going to miss every part of this experience. If you have haters — you've been around long enough to have a hater — that means you're doing something really, really well. I've been lucky enough. I will say, I'm not cut out for public scrutiny. This is not something for me. This will be my last reality show.

No Traitors in your future then?

I mean, they come knocking. Of course, I'll open the door. But at least for Traitors , they're going to take my phone. No, but it's great. I've been lucky enough to make it this far, and it's just part of the competition. We got a couple days left.

The season 35 finale of Dancing With the Stars airs Tuesday at 5 p.m. PT/8 p.m. ET, simulcasting across ABC and Disney+ and streaming the next day on Hulu . Check out all of The Hollywood Reporter ’s DWTS coverage here .

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google With the Avengers: Doomsday release date drawing ever closer, the reveals just keep coming, and now, that has included a brand-new Doomsday teaser that shows previously unseen footage of two original Avengers facing off against Doctor Doom. Already, this week has brought a shocking number of Doomsday updates, most notably the final Doomsday trailer , which prominently featured Steve Rogers, confirming, among other things, that Steve and Bucky will finally reunite and that he has a somewhat grown son (who looks to be about preteen age).

On the heels of that trailer and the fanfare that followed it, a new Entertainment Weekly article comprised a number of updates and reveals, to an explanation for why certain X-Men are missing from Doomsday to new insight about Doctor Doom from Robert Downey Jr. , specifically regarding the differences between Tony Stark/Iron Man and Doom. As if that wasn't exciting enough, this new teaser for Doomsday is showing some all new looks at the film, including a showdown that fans will no doubt be eager to see. Check out the teaser and more about this upcoming face-off below.

It doesn't really come as any surprise that Steve Rogers and Thor will be facing off against Doctor Doom in Doomsday . After all, we've already seen that Thor and Doom go head to head in prior trailers for the movie, and with Steve clearly being such a central figure, especially following that most recent trailer, it was only a matter of time. Even so, it's cool to get a first look at that actual meeting (assuming that this is the first meeting) in the teaser, which shows Thor and Steve together approaching Doom and his throne.

New international teaser for ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’ In theaters on December 18. pic.twitter.com/poFeuTql8Q

However, this teaser also comes as a reminder that the Avengers really do have an uphill battle in this movie. In addition to Doctor Doom's power, which is already known to be immense and world-ending, Doom currently has both the Hulk and the Scarlet Witch on his side, following the post-credits scenes in Spider-Man: Brand New Day and VisionQuest , respectively. We also don't yet know who the other Latverian witches are, assuming that Wanda Maximoff is one of them, which feels like a safe bet at this point, and it's possible that Doom has collected other characters, like Spider-Man and even Doctor Strange.

With all of that in mind, and considering Thor's unfortunate line in the Doomsday trailer about him not even knowing half of the heroes present, this feels like an even more impossible task than the fight against Thanos in Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame . And, considering that Avengers: Secret Wars is already confirmed to be releasing next year, it seems like the Avengers will probably lose before they win, not unlike those aforementioned movies.

Do you think the Avengers have a chance against Doom? Let us know (and why) in the comments below.

articles.title: Christopher Nolan's Mind-Bending Thriller That Is Better Than Inception Is Being Erased from Netflix
articles.summary: Courtesy of Summit Entertainment Christopher Nolan has become renowned as one of the best directors working in Hollywood, and along with his work on movies like Oppenheimer, the Dark Knight Trilogy, and his epic take on The Odyssey, Nolan has made some of the most narratively mind-bending movies of the last three decades. All the way back in 2000, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Christopher Nolan has become renowned as one of the best directors working in Hollywood, and along with his work on movies like Oppenheimer , the Dark Knight Trilogy, and his epic take on The Odyssey , Nolan has made some of the most narratively mind-bending movies of the last three decades. All the way back in 2000, long before he would receive his first Oscar or be granted $250 million budgets, the director make his first major impact on the industry with a movie with a fractured story that really made audiences pay attention to what was happening on screen. That movie was Memento , starring Guy Pearce as a man with memory loss , who attempts to piece together a sequence of events to uncover the mystery of how he ended up in the position he is in when viewers first join his story. For those who have not seen the movie, or simply want to revisit it, if you are a Netflix subscriber your time to do so is running out as the movie leaves the platform on December 1.

Memento centers on Leonard Shelby, who suffers from anterograde amnesia after an attack that led to the death of his wife. His memories of the life he had before the attack are intact, but new memories only stay with him for a short time before he forgets them. On a quest for vengeance against his wife's killer, Leonard builds a map of Polaroids, notes and body tattoos to help him piece together the events that he can no longer remember and finally get his revenge. While this could sound like a regular film with a simple storyline of a wronged man on a road to ruin, Nolan's genius move is to tell the story across two timelines in a piece of fractured storytelling that puts viewers into the life of Leonard and his distorted memories.

Many years after making Memento , Christopher Nolan would completely baffle audiences with his reality-twisting Inception , but the same kind of highly detailed direction and plotting was all there way back in his first big hit. Memento breaks the story of Leonard into two distinctive timelines; one in black and white showing Leonard taking a phone call in motel room and one in color, told in stages in reverse chronological order that slowly piece together the mystery of the film in the same way Leonard recalls them. The movie concludes with the two timelines converging in a final revelation and bringing to a conclusion one of the most riveting and accomplished movies of Nolan's career despite his subsequent huge successes.

The movie was made for just $9 million and easily became a hit with a $48 million box office return. As well as being hailed as a masterpiece in storytelling by both critics and audiences (with Rotten Tomatoes scores of 93% and 94% respectively), the film also received Academy Awards nods for Best Original Screenplay and Best Editing, the latter of these really being what made the movie what it is. It also established a blueprint that Nolan would utilize frequently in his movies, with fractured storytelling, manipulation of time, and emotional-driven lead protagonists playing a part in many movies such as Tenet , Dunkirk, and, of course, Inception . However, it is hard to imagine any of those movies without Memento . For anyone who has not seen the film, it is certainly worth seeking out on Netflix before the end of the month, and while it may not get you in the Christmas mood, you will get a movie a that is hard to forget.

Is Memento still one of Christopher Nolan's best movies? Let us know what you think in the comments.

He was 91. His death was announced by his nephew, Alan Rosenberg. Rosenberg's first film job was as design assistant on the […]
articles.content:
Philip Rosenberg, a production designer and art director who was part of the team that won the art direction-set decoration Oscar for " All That Jazz ," died Oct. 28 in West Palm Beach, Florida. He was 91.

His death was announced by his nephew, Alan Rosenberg.

Rosenberg's first film job was as design assistant on the 1968 "The Sea Gull." He went on to become an art director and production designer, working with New York-based directors such as Sidney Lumet, Paul Mazursky and Norman Jewison. He partnered with production designer Tony Walton on films including "The Wiz" and "All That Jazz." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Chris Colfer Says 'Glee' Reboot 'Conversations' About Kurt's Return Are Ongoing: 'From What I Heard, It Sounded Very Funny and Like a Good Idea' Jane Lynch Wants to Return for 'Glee' Reboot: 'I Would Love to Do Sue Sylvester for the Rest of My Life'

Known for being part of the realist school of production design in the 1970s, he was nominated for an Oscar as art director of "The Wiz." Among his other credits were "The Owl and the Pussycat," "Next Stop Greenwich Village," "The Gambler," "Network," "The Sentinel," "Running on Empty," "Night Falls on Manhattan" and "Moonstruck." His final credit came for "Collateral Damage" in 2002.

Rosenberg grew up in Prospect Park South, Flatbush, Brooklyn, and studied scenic design at Yale. After graduation, he was hired as an assistant at the Metropolitan Opera, as well as assisting Marcel Vertès on the murals in the Cafe Carlyle.

He married Siv Sandstrom, a hostess in the Swedish pavilion at the 1964 World's Fair, who assisted him in the art department on films including "Running on Empty" and "Moonstruck." She died in 2024.

He is survived by his brothers Stanley Rosenberg and David Rosenberg and six nieces and nephews.

articles.title: One of the 80s' Most Inappropriate Superheroes Somehow Got His Own Children's Toy Line
articles.summary: The Toxic Avenger is tasteless, crass, and about the last thing you'd expect to see propping up a toy line for children. But somehow, Playmates decided to turn Toxie into an action figure line with 1991's Toxic Crusaders, tying in to the just-as-inexplicable Toxic Crusaders cartoon that aired a brief thirteen episode season that same […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Toxic Avenger is tasteless, crass, and about the last thing you'd expect to see propping up a toy line for children. But somehow, Playmates decided to turn Toxie into an action figure line with 1991's Toxic Crusaders , tying in to the just-as-inexplicable Toxic Crusaders cartoon that aired a brief thirteen episode season that same year. Who thought this was a good idea? A clue lies within the manufacturer of the Toxic Crusaders toyline: Playmates. In 1988, Playmates had a surprise monster hit with their Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles action figure line, which was still the most popular action figure line on the market in 1991. With its similar premise of "mutant hero born out of toxic waste," it wasn't that far-fetched to imagine kids having a similar response to The Toxic Avenger . And while the source-material from Troma wasn't exactly kid-friendly, neither were the original Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles comics from Mirage. The series and its toys may not have lasted long, but like everything else ever to emerge from Tromaville, they have built a dedicated cult following.

No definitive reason has ever been settled on for what happened to the Toxic Crusaders series and figures. Alternately, controversy over the R-rated source material and general marketplace oversaturation have been blamed: the early nineties were a golden age for both intellectual-property based cartoon series and tie-in toylines. The expansion of cable television meant that there were now far more networks with competing children's programming, inspiring series we're still talking about today . Most of them, however, met the same fate as Toxic Crusaders , lasting for only a season and condemning their tie-in toylines to languish on-shelves. The Playmates Toxic Crusaders line was not a strong seller, but the enduring cult popularity of the Toxic Avenger toyline has given it a second-life with action figure collectors, who are willing to pay a premium for rare, end-of-line release like the Apocalypse Attackcopter vehicle .

Nine figures and five vehicles were produced for the Toxic Crusaders line. With their neon-colors and gross-out sculpts, the resemblance to Playmates' Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles line is unmistakeable. The good guy faction was headed up by the Toxic Avenger himself, joined by Major Disaster, Nozone, Headbanger, and Junkyard. The line's four villains were led by Doctor Killemoff, joined by henchmen Psycho, Bonehead, and the Radiation Ranger. Each figure came packaged with a special glow-in-the-dark accessory, which came sealed in a plastic bag, labeled "SECRET TOXIC GLOW-IN-THE-DARK WEAPON: SO RADIOACTIVE WE'VE PUT IT UNDER WRAPS." Three to five additional weapons and accessories were included with each figure, finding them complete poses a significant challenge to collectors today. Especially sought-after is the Toxic Avenger's signature mop, without which the figure just doesn't look right.

Nozone is the most "gross-out" character in the line, featuring an exaggeratedly-giant nose (hence the name), as well as sculpted splatters of snot all over the figure. He's a former test pilot, mutated by flying through a hole in the ozone layer. After a crash-landing into a radioactive silo filled with pepper, the toxic chemicals in Nozone's body grant him the mutant ability to produce powerful sneezes. Tongue was firmly in-cheek when these characters were created, to be certain. Headbanger's origin calls DC's Firestorm to mind, while his design evokes Masters of the Universe 's Two-Bad : a scientist and a singing telegram fall into an atom-smasher, merging into a single being. Headbanger is at first one of Doctor Killemoff's henchmen, but switches sides after discovering the Toxic Crusaders get more dates (really). Junkyard is also the result of a fusion, a half-man, half-dog created by lightning-striking a toxic waste contaminated homeless man and his pet. Major Disaster is comparatively bland: he's a soldier who gains the ability to control plants from a radioactive swamp, a little like Man-Thing or Swamp Thing .

Doctor Killemoff is a native of the planet Smogula, trying to terraform (Smogulaform?) Earth into a polluted world akin to his ravished home-planet. He wears a breathing apparatus, depicted as an elaborate, multi-piece accessory, to help him survive in Earth's toxic fresh air. Psycho is his bio-mechanoid lackey, and possesses powers of prognostication that go ignored by his master: every episode, Psycho is able to accurately predict how the Toxic Crusaders will foil their plans. Bonehead is an acid-rain scarred punk and former enemy of the pre-transformation Toxic Avenger, now anointed commander of the "Radiation Rangers," Killemoff's force of mutant foot soldiers. Additional villain characters like the monstrous "Polluto" were featured in the series, though the toyline was cancelled before they could be given a plastic counterpart.

Somehow, Toxic Crusaders occupied the confluence of three trends. Most immediately, there was an early nineties trend of environmentally-conscious children's cartoons, with these themes cropping up in Captain Planet and the Planeteers and Swamp Thing as well as Toxic Crusaders . Besides Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, it was the prevalence of these series that convinced Troma and their partners to move ahead with Toxic Crusaders . The other trends were longer-term, and less easily explained. Beginning in the mid-eighties with series like Rambo: The Force of Freedom and RoboCop , animation studios and TV networks looked to R-rated film properties to provide recognizable franchise names for their children's series. The principle made sense: R-rated franchises and characters had the allure of "forbidden fruit" to children, and these series would let them see them in action. Other times, companies like Kenner would go ahead with a kid-ified version of a property like Aliens or Predator without a tie-in series, trading on the existing adult name of the franchise alone. There was a somehow-unforeseen drawback: parents.

The parents of these children were also familiar with properties like Aliens, RoboCop , and The Toxic Avenger, and it's been suggested they played a key role in the demise of these toylines and cartoons. Although largely apocryphal, the contention is that parents just weren't comfortable with these grown-up franchises being marketed to their kids, and wouldn't buy the toys or let them watch the tie-in. The most significant backlash was seen in the late eighties, when parent groups successfully had several companies' Nightmare on Elm Street children's toys discontinued. However, these factors also contribute to the aftermarket for these toys, drawing adult collectors them decades later. Some are just fans of the property, fascinated by the sheer weirdness of Toxic Avenger action figures. Others are those same kids whose parents wouldn't let them collect the line back in 1991, finally making good on the desires of their eight-year-old self. Either way, Toxic Crusaders has become one of the stranger footnotes of its era, forgotten by most toy collectors, but passionately collected by a dedicated cult following.

articles.title: Demon Slayer Peaked Early, But Infinity Castle Can Save It
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Ufotable The Demon Slayer anime peaked early thanks to its first season and movie, but the series still has the potential to surpass that success. The reason for its early success wasn't its epic storytelling but rather Ufotable's fascinating anime adaptation. The studio captivated anime fans worldwide with its vibrant animation, showcasing modern animation at its […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Demon Slayer anime peaked early thanks to its first season and movie, but the series still has the potential to surpass that success. The reason for its early success wasn't its epic storytelling but rather Ufotable's fascinating anime adaptation. The studio captivated anime fans worldwide with its vibrant animation, showcasing modern animation at its peak. However, what followed after the first season was the anime movie adaptation of the next canon arc from the manga, which is where the series truly peaked. It showcased a level of animation that surpassed everything else up until then.

First released in Japanese theaters in late 2020, the anime movie became a huge success. With the manga also approaching its conclusion at the time, the movie boosted manga sales exponentially, helping the series reach 150 million copies in total sales. Since then, the series has gained another 70 million copies in sales, surpassing 220 million as of this writing . However, despite two more seasons and another movie, the series has yet to match the heights it reached early on. The Infinity Castle trilogy, however, can surpass that achievement by building on what the franchise has already accomplished, and it is already doing so.

Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle was a huge success for the franchise and at the box office, earning more than $200 million compared to Mugen Train . On paper, this already suggests that it is a bigger success than its predecessor. However, the main element Infinity Castle had going for it was its animation, which, despite being an improvement, was something fans had already come to expect. Many fans even believed that the movie should have been an anime season instead, as it essentially felt like nine episodes consolidated into a single film. That said, while its emotional impact may have fallen short compared to Rengoku's death, the first movie has laid the foundation for what is to come next.

This is exactly what makes the next two movies' potential to surpass it and reach even greater heights so exciting. The second movie will likely include two major events, potentially featuring the battles against Upper Moon Ranks One and Two. Once again, this could make the second movie feel like an entire season compiled into a single film. If that happens, the final installment, featuring the all-out battle against Muzan, could be the one that truly feels like a movie. As the final installment in the Demon Slayer franchise, it has the potential to elevate the series to even greater heights, surpassing what it has already achieved.

In other ways, the Demon Slayer franchise has already excelled, from its animation to its compelling and emotional storytelling. To surpass that foundation, bringing the climax to the big screen is what could truly solidify the franchise's legacy as a visual masterpiece. The Demon Slayer franchise is already on a different level , having reached heights that fans might not have expected it to surpass. However, if the franchise aims to go even further and save itself as an anime that will be remembered for more than just its animation, it will need to stick the landing with its final film, something the concluding installment of the anime has the potential to achieve.

articles.title: HBO's Harry Potter Reboot Confirms Big Change From the Movie Costumes That's Book Accurate
articles.summary: HBO HBO's Harry Potter TV series will be the Christmas present that the entire world gets this year, and hopefully it's one they want to keep. The series will offer a long-form version of what a generation of fans got from the Harry Potter films, and (hopefully) will take readers of the books on a much […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google HBO's Harry Potter TV series will be the Christmas present that the entire world gets this year, and hopefully it's one they want to keep. The series will offer a long-form version of what a generation of fans got from the Harry Potter films, and (hopefully) will take readers of the books on a much more complete and familiar journey. As the premiere date gets closer, we're seeing much more of what the finished production looks like, and diehard fans are spotting some pretty fine details that show the level of fidelity the show is showing to the text.

The latest set of Harry Potter promotional images showcases a milestone moment from the first novel, Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone : Harry Potter's first trip to Diagon Alley, the hidden magical market where all Wizards and Witches go to shop for their mystic essentials. However, fans are also taking note of something else in the image: the fashion Harry is wearing before he gets some proper wizard's robes.

The official Harry Potter website posted a new featured article titled "Six fashionable findings from the HBO Original Harry Potter series costume department". It helps viewers get a deeper sense of the intense level of detail that was put into the show. The first item on the list is "How to spot magical people in the Muggle world," and it features the above image of Harry Potter (actor Dominic McLaughlin) taking in the wonder of Diagon Alley, while wearing an outfit that very much looks like what a '90s kid would be wearing.

In the breakdown, the style and design team behind Harry Potter describe how they had to create a sense of fashion for the Wizarding World that felt like it could plausibly exist alongside the fashion of non-magic humans (or "Muggles") of the time. That meant "a lot of synthetics. The costume department scoured charity shops and rag-and-bone yards, consulting their family albums for unglamourous ensembles to represent early 90s fashion: unfiltered."

There's also an interesting amount of logic that went into guiding the style choices for the series: "Magical people don’t stick to trends," the site states. "They would likely ditch high street shops for jumble sales, culminating in more eclectic, unconventional wardrobes. Don’t expect all witches and wizards to look the same."

There's an even deeper dive into the fashion of Harry Potter (2026), check it out on the franchise's official site .

The Harry Potter movies that Warner Bros. put out started in 2001 with Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone , and ended in 2011 with Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2 . The studio chose to update the story to a modern-day setting (at that time), meaning that characters wore 2000s fashion trends to make them relatable to audience members of similar age. It raised some ire with hardcore fans of the books, as there are some deeper metaphors and symbolism about real-world politics and culture at that time, which were invariably altered by the time shift.

Now, the TV series is going the opposite route with its period piece format. It'll be interesting to see how viewers react to that, and if the book-accurate setting really does change or enhance the experience of the story, in visual form.

Harry Potter will premiere on HBO on Christmas Day. Do you like the '90s look?

articles.title: Charles Barkley Pitched His Potential Inside The NBA Replacement, But I Have Another Idea
articles.summary: This isn't a bad pick, but another host is on my mind.
articles.content:
As Inside the NBA ’s latest season on ESPN continues, questions continue to swirl around the show in regard to its future. Longtime co-host Ernie Johnson has officially confirmed his plans to leave the show at the end of this season, and colleague Charles Barkley apparently plans to do the same. There’s been a lot of discussion regarding who might replace the beloved sports commentators, and Barkley recently pitched his successor. While it’s a solid pick, I’d admittedly prefer to see another seasoned pundit take over Barkley’s post.

Barkley – also known as “The Round Mound of Rebound” to some – is definitely someone who loves to speak his mind. So it doesn’t surprise me at all that he’d have thoughts on who might be able to take his place on Inside . The former Phoenix Sun was recently quoted as saying he didn’t believe anyone but fellow ex-player Jalen Rose could replace him at the desk. That comment was brought up to Rose when he was interviewed by Front Office Sports (as seen on YouTube ) and, when asked about the job, he said this:

The notion of Rose taking over for Barkley is actually quite reasonable, considering his resume as a broadcaster. He’s not only served as a fill-in analyst for Inside the NBA for years now, but he’s also taken on hosting duties for ABC/ESPN over the years. I personally enjoy seeing Rose when he appears on Inside , and his relaxed demeanor usually serves as a firm counterbalance to others on the dais like the vivacious Barkley or Shaquille O’Neal . With that said, there’s another recurring analyst I’d love to see join the show instead.

Inside has welcomed plenty of insightful and entertaining guest hosts over the years, from the cool Vince Carter to the wise-cracking Draymond Green (who has a rivalry with Charles Barkley) . Someone who, for me, has always been a welcome presence on the show is Chris Webber, who’s been appearing on the show for years. He obviously has plenty of broadcasting experience, and he’s a wealth of knowledge when it comes to basketball. I’d say the show would be lucky to have him full-time.

Again, though, this isn’t to say that Jalen Rose wouldn’t be able to do the job effectively. There may actually be a reality in which both players end up on the show full time by next season. However, that’s assuming ESPN is looking to bring on two former players and not get another non-ex-player analyst to specifically fill the void that’ll be left by Johnson.

To be honest, it may also behoove me not to get too ahead of myself right now, as the season is still young. Also, while Charles Barkley’s retirement claim is seeming more likely , he hasn’t said much more about it in the wake of Ernie Johnson’s announcement. We’ll just have to wait and see what happens and how the producers choose to proceed should Barkley leave the fold along with Johnson.

articles.title: Charlie Brown's Thanksgiving Special Isn't Good, But There Are 5 Reasons To Still Watch it
articles.summary: A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving from 1973 is arguably among the least thrilling of the Peanuts' animated antics, especially from the retro era of the cartoon. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving from 1973 is arguably among the least thrilling of the Peanuts' animated antics, especially from the retro era of the cartoon. Even Charlie Brown himself seems tired of his holiday specials, remorsefully lamenting to Linus, "We've got another holiday to worry about." While I agree with his sister Sally's complaints about how she has barely finished her Halloween candy, this cartoon offers very few memorable gags and seems more contrived than it does original. What it lacks in standing out among its dozens of peers , it makes up for it in a few ways that shockingly make it worth the watch.

Charlie Brown is off to visit his Grandmother to celebrate with his family, but his plans are interrupted by Peppermint Patty when she invites herself over to his home to spend the holiday. He finds himself in an even worse predicament when his guest list grows from one classmate to many more, and he's forced to figure out how to entertain and feed an entire cavalcade of kids. As if the general feeling of existential dread and anxiety that Charlie Brown walks around with on a daily basis wasn't enough, now he has to figure out how to roast a turkey when all he knows how to do is burn toast and pour milk on cereal. It sounds straightforward, and it is — but the road to that festive meal includes a handful of elements that make this Thanksgiving cartoon something to add in your holiday viewing rotation.

Peppermint Patty is an iconic part of the Peanuts cast, but she wasn't an original one when the strip debuted back in 1950 (although there was someone named Patty but these two characters are not the same). It wasn't until Aug. 1966 that the green-shirted brunette first stepped her sandals onto newspaper strips. This was the same year that It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown! first hit the airwaves on CBS, but there would be six more animated specials in between this Thanksgiving toon before we finally saw her in an animated format.

A friend of "Chuck's" as she prefers to call him, Peppermint Patty inserted herself into Charlie Brown's Thanksgiving plans rather abruptly, but in her mind she was entitled to his attention. Throughout her time in the series, Patty has shown an interest in the yellow-shirted blockhead that goes beyond friendship. She's very forward with him on the phone, leaving him blushing and at a loss for words. While it isn't shown in this special, Patty's companion Marcie also has a crush on the same guy — something he has zero ability to handle. Charlie Brown is not much for romance and is the furthest thing from a casanova, so it's funny to watch him in these situations where he probably enjoys the attention from a girl but has no idea what to do with it.

Vince Guaraldi had been working with Charles Schulz and the Peanuts gang as far back as 1963, predating the first animated Christmas special. Alongside his trio and later quintet, Guaraldi composed and played his jazz stylings through a dozen Charlie Brown cartoons, with this one among the group. If the Christmas soundtrack was more melancholy and the Halloween special a bit more serious and spooky, the Thanksgiving special is more upbeat and light-hearted to match the nature of its story.

Guaraldi's updated reprise of "Linus and Lucy" for Snoopy's cooking montage is a jam that keeps on giving, adding more flair to one of his most well-known jazz compositions that has become the theme song for the franchise. Where the soundtrack shines the most is "Little Birdie," a song that introduces Woodstock into the mix during this toon. The majority of Guaraldi's work on the series were instrumental, but "Little Birdie" is one of the few songs across the series that has lyrics, but one of a very tiny selection that the artist sang by himself. His expressive and soulful voice backed by sounds of brass and bass is extremely catchy and will stick with you long after the memory of the cartoon disappears.

There are some pretty solid visual gags throughout the Thanksgiving show, including one of my favorite sequences with Snoopy brawling against a lawn chair in a clash of champions that is not as one-sided as you might think. But throughout the entire show, it's Woodstock who steals the show as the funniest element that keeps the audience laughing and wondering what he will do next. It's impossible not to love the tiny yellow bird, and he adds a ton of comedy relief alongside Snoopy. Their relationship is often more Laurel & Hardy, with Snoopy using his size to make some jokes about their power dynamic, but Woodstock always shines and makes sure both buddies come out on top.

Besides helping Snoopy cook the non-traditional Thanksgiving meal (more on that in a second), Woodstock joined his pal in dressing up as pilgrims in a very silly segment that involves a luggage trunk and some oversized hats. If Snoopy and Woodstock came from overseas to colonize my people, I'd be a little less apprehensive about it than a ship full of British people. Woodstock simply makes everything better, and he was another great addition to the Peanuts roster that brought a ton of energy to this otherwise bland affair.

Since Charlie Brown is catering a meal for kids who aren't allowed to use a stove without parental guidance, he does the rational thing and employs his dog and bird friend to do all the cooking. Snoopy puts on his adorable chefs hat and gets to work, making popcorn and buttered toast to accompany their side dishes of jellybeans and pretzel sticks. If you were a child making dinner who had no idea how to cook, this is basically what you would do. Anyone can operate a toaster, even a canine who may or may not have opposable thumbs.

Snoopy would make Martha Stewart proud, decorating a ping-pong table with a lovely linen cloth and origami-folded napkins. While it's all very nice, what upsets me is Snoopy's lack of beverages for the kids. Mysterious pink sundae cups appear on the table during the feast with no explanation (and we're never shown who made them or what they actually are), so we can assume whatever cherry-topped concoction in there is in place of their drinks. If I was eating all that salt, dry bread and tooth-decaying snacks, I'd want something to sip on, but we can only expect so much. After all, Snoopy needed time to work on his pilgrim costume with Woodstock. He has his priorities, but we appreciate him making the time and putting in the effort to feed this makeshift group.

Peppermint Patty might think Charlie Brown is cute, but her patience for his spontaneous Thanksgiving party is practically non-existent. Besides inviting herself over without asking, Patty rudely complains to the entire party about the meal and berates him in front of the guests. It isn't until Marcie reminds her compatriot that she was never actually asked to come, and may have hurt his feelings with her brusque words. Charlie Brown takes it to heart and worries he ruined Thanksgiving for everyone, but Marcie reminds him that they should all be thankful to be together while Patty apologizes for playing "lover's games" and the group reconcile.

In the end, all of the kids are invited to Charlie Brown's grandmother's condo to celebrate Thanksgiving. Meanwhile, Snoopy and Woodstock stay home and enjoy a secret traditional meal with the yellow bird eating one of his distant cousins with a smile. That might be the most memorable thing about this special, but I'm choosing to ignore that one because I don't want to have Charlie Brown levels of anxiety thinking about Woodstock as a cannibal. But what should stay with you more is how the ultimate message in this cartoon was a very practical lesson in gratitude. The main course is "Be happy with what you have and not what you don't" with a side of "friends are family," differentiating it from other Thanksgiving specials that focus on just the general idea of being thankful. It's a bit more nuanced and surprisingly mature for a kids cartoon, but we shouldn't expect less from a boy named Charlie Brown.

Do you have any memories of the Charlie Brown Thanksgiving special, or maybe a different nostalgic cartoon about Turkey Day? Join the conversation and let us know in the comments below.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Bungie has created one of its best cinematic trailers yet for Marathon's newest Shell, Bishop, which is saying a lot considering how great the studio is at these. Each Shell trailer showcases the character, but this is easily one of the most impressive and stylish. In it, Bungie reveals Bishop, a striking new Shell that immediately gives samurai robot vibes. There is no doubt this Shell will be a popular pick once it drops as part of Marathon's Symbiote update and future plans. The trailer teases some possible aspects of the Shell's kit, but we won't know its full capabilities just yet.

Bishop was previously teased as part of Marathon 's upcoming Symbiosis update , which is scheduled to launch on December 8. However, Bungie's latest cinematic offers a much better understanding of the playstyle the developer wants to encourage with the new Runner Shell. While most players would probably want to maintain some distance between themselves and their enemies in an extraction shooter, Bishop appears to thrive in close-quarters combat. Between its intimidating appearance, incredible speed, and devastating melee capabilities, the new Shell looks like something ripped straight out of a samurai fan's dreams, and that's certainly not a bad thing for Bungie's shooter.

Bungie shared the new Bishop Shell cinematic on November 24, accompanied by the tagline, "BISHOP SHELL // HUNTER KILLER. STRIKE ONCE, STRIKE FAST." Sporting a striking red chassis, an extendable blade, and leg-mounted thrusters, Bishop systematically hunts down an opposing crew throughout the trailer. The robot uses firearms alongside throwing knives, showing the diversity of its kit.

However, it's the closing moments of the cinematic that really steal the show. After being shot by an opportunistic Rook, Bishop lowers itself into a combat stance, extends its blade, and uses its thrusters to rapidly dash toward its opponent, delivering a devastating melee strike reminiscent of classic samurai films. If this is anything to go by, Bishop could be exactly the shakeup Bungie needs to keep Marathon interesting and afloat .

Mobility is king in Marathon and Bishop appears to have that in spades. It could be great at crossing open areas, and extremely deadly when fighting inside buildings or navigating narrow corridors. An aggressive Bishop player could potentially close the distance before an opponent has time to reposition, making encounters particularly unpredictable.

Of course, the cinematic isn't representative of actual gameplay, and Bungie has yet to fully detail Bishop's abilities, cooldowns, or damage output. Balancing such a mobile, melee-focused character will undoubtedly be important. Bishop is also just one reason to be excited about Marathon 's Symbiosis update. Bungie is introducing Expedition, a permanent PvE mode featuring roguelite elements, alongside an experimental 3v3 Team Deathmatch mode. Marathon's future is looking up , and Bishop is just one part of that.

As summer draws to a close, the theatrical release of Children of Blood and Bone draws nearer.

The film adaptation of Tomi Adeyemi’s YA fantasy is directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood , and it stars quite a stacked cast of actors and characters.

For everything we know about the Children of Blood and Bone movie, read on.

When will Gina Prince-Bythewood’s Children of Blood and Bone come out?

Thuso Mbedu , who worked with both director Prince-Bythewood and costar Viola Davis on The Woman King (2022), will star as the main character Zelie. Amandla Stenberg ( The Hate U Give , The Acolyte ) will portray Amari. Damson Idris ( F1 , Snowfall ) will play Inan. Tosin Cole ( Supacell ) will portray Tzain.

Davis will portray Mama Agba. Cynthia Erivo ( Wicked ) will portray Admiral Kaea. Idris Elba ( Fast & Furious Presents: Hobbs & Shaw ) will play Lekan. Saniyya Sidney ( Fences ),  Zackary Momoh  ( Harriet ), Richard Mofe-Damijo ( Namaste Wahala ), Ayra Starr, Pamilerin Ayodeji ( Mikolo ), Shamz Garuba ( Crime and Justice Lagos ), Kola Bodunde ( Shadow ) and Temi Fagbenle rounded out the cast later on. Ayodeji and Garuba were cast through an open casting call in Nigeria.

Is there a trailer for the Children of Blood and Bone movie?

Yes, a trailer was released in late July, introducing the cast and their characters as Orïsha faces a battle for its magic. Another trailer was released in early November along with artists who have contributed songs to the film. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

What is Children of Blood and Bone about?

The first novel in the Legacy of Orïsha trilogy chronicles Zelie's journey to restore the intrinsic magic to the land after King Saran made a move to purge it, seeing it as a threat and unnatural. Drawning on African mythology, the fantasy setting contains groups of humans that practice magic known as Maji. The Maji divine certain elements, and thus are known by the specific powers they wield, from water workers beckoning tides to those like Zelie's mother Jumoke, who can summon souls.

Zelie and her brother team up with the son and daughter of King Saran. Prince Inan (Idris) has doubts about taking on his father's crown and following King Saran's example directly.

What artists will have music in the upcoming Children of Blood and Bone movie?

Tems serves as the soundtrack executive producer, and has contributed "African Love Song" which is featured in the film's second trailer. Beyoncé's "Energy (feat. Beam)" featured in the first trailer. Guest features on the soundtrack include:

Adeyemi co-wrote the screenplay with Prince-Bythewood. She has expressed that she won’t watch the film, and she posted a video on Instagram explaining her experience on set.

Are there more Children of Blood and Bone books? Will there be more movies?

Yes, the book gave way to a trilogy. Following Children of Blood and Bone 's publish date in 2018, Children of Virtue and Vengeance arrived in 2019, and Children of Anguish and Anarchy arrived in 2024.

There are currently no plans to adapt the next two books in the series into films.

Adeyemi has The Siren coming out at the end of September.

articles.content:
Wu-Tang Clan has big plans for Thanksgiving. The hip-hop legends will be in Detroit to headline the halftime show for the NFL game between the host Lions and the Chicago Bears (U2 will do the halftime honors for the Thanksgiving Eve game in LA between the Green Bay Packers and the Los Angeles Rams, airing on Netflix ).

Wu-Tang, founded in Staten Island, NY, has long been considered one of the most influential groups in music history, with legions of fans worldwide and even their own acolytes known as the Killa Bees, a collective of rappers, producers, singers and others affiliated with the group. Among the most notable Bees: Cilvaringz , aka Tarik Azzougarh , a Dutch Moroccan Wu-Tang superfan turned artist whose connection to the Clan goes back to the late 1990s. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The remarkable story of how Cilvaringz became associated with Wu-Tang and then played a critical role in producing the astonishing one-copy only album Once Upon a Time in Shaolin is told in the documentary The Disciple: A Wu-Tang Fable , now streaming on Netflix. Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

The Oscar-contending film is directed by Joanna Natasegara, the Academy Award-winning producer of The White Helmets , The Edge of Democracy , Virunga and other acclaimed documentaries. The Disciple premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January and screened in September at the Telluride Film Festival before debuting on Netflix.

DEADLINE: Have you always been into Wu-Tang? When did you learn about the story of Tarik Azzougarh?

Joanna Natasegara: I grew up in the '90s. It's exactly my era of music… Wu-Tang was just something me and my friends were very much into. We would go to clubs and listen to hip hop music, but it was something I just didn't really think about in the scope of my work, clearly for decades, actually. And so, the story [of Tarik/Cilvaringz] itself I hadn't heard of despite it being something that had gone around the world. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I was on a holiday in Morocco with my family and a script writer friend of mine came for lunch and she said, “My brother [Tarik] is having some trouble with his life story and his life rights.” And I was like, “Okay.” I knew he was Moroccan, but I thought [his story] would be something that pertained to North Africa, not to Staten Island. And she said, “Do you know the Wu-Tang?” I was like, “Yeah. I don't really know where this is going.” [She said], “He's a Killer Bee.” And I was like, “How is that possible?” And so, she told me a little part of the story, but she said, “It's so convoluted, complicated, twisty, wonderful. Can I bring him to lunch tomorrow?”

So, he came to lunch and honestly, over a three-hour lunch, he told me his whole life story. And not only did I think it was a great story, it just really resonated. We're exactly the same age. He was obviously a migrant growing up in a tiny town in Europe, and a lot of that resonated with me and he was very ambitious to make it [in the music business], and I thought that was really inspiring.

DEADLINE: It's a very complex story to tell as your feature directorial debut. About halfway into The Disciple , you really start to pivot to the sale of the kind of one-off album, Once Upon a Time in Shaolin . But as an audience we really need to understand how it all came together. We need to understand Cilvaringz, Tarik, and that's complicated. So, this is not an easy piece of storytelling to do.

JN: No, no, no, it wasn't… I wanted to build the film as a kind of homage to a Wu-Tang album. There's a lot of Easter eggs in the film — if you're a Clan fan, you can see them. But I also wanted the film to work for somebody that didn't know anything about the Wu-Tang. So that's a tricky balance to be able to tell a story that's not too complex, but also dense enough for the mega fans, and there are millions of them.

I was well held by two extremely experienced editors, Chloe Lambourne who cut for For Sama and Chris Dickens who cut for Slumdog Millionaire . And that was a lot of fun.

DEADLINE: The film does work for people who are not steeped in either hip hop or Wu-Tang or martial arts movies or “pharma bro” Martin Shkreli [who bought the one-copy only album] or other elements of the story.

JN: It's a coming-of-age story and a story about ambition because I think that's what Tarik took from RZA, what RZA took from Shifu [Shaolin monk Shi Yan Ming] and what audiences are seeming to take from Tarik. So, the album in a way is kind of a McGuffin. Obviously, some people are very attracted to know about the machinations of the album, but I'm really interested in the mentorship aspect of the film.

DEADLINE: There's the line that RZA says: “Persistence overcomes resistance,” and it's wonderful. That motto guided Tarik as a protégé of RZA and Wu-Tang, but it could also apply to you as a filmmaker.

JN: It's great, isn't it? We had t-shirts made.

DEADLINE: Towards the end of the film, you ask Tarik specifically whether producing Once Upon a Time in Shaolin was a career highlight or if it destroyed his career. And his answer is quite interesting, that he doesn't necessarily think of himself as having a career.

JN: I think he's quite honest and reflective in the piece. I thank him for that trust because that's important, isn't it, in documentary? And I think he is reflective about that process, but he's also resilient and knew what that meant to do that [album]. I think they both did, him and RZA, but the discussion [it ignited] was the point [about the value attached to a work of music] and that has worked. People are seeing that stunt and the value of music because of it. And I think it's inspired many other people to do similar things. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

The album was a perfect protest. It was a perfect way to say, why is this piece of music worth less than something that is put in an extraordinary museum? So, I think it was a really clever protest piece, and to that extent it's also worked. We're talking about it years later. So, it's a conversation that's endured and I think is really relevant not only to music now, but also to film or any piece of creative, especially as we move more and more into the dangers of AI. How much less will everything be valued, in fact?

Note: After Martin Shkreli’s conviction for fraud, the U.S. government seized his assets, including the one copy of Once Upon a Time in Shaolin encased in its custom-made box. Per a legal agreement, the album will not be available for commercial release until the year 2103. In the interim, it can only be played at limited special events.

DEADLINE: Probably the first question you get asked is, have you listened to the album?

JN: We had a beautiful listening session at Sundance, and then we had another one at Telluride. I haven't heard the whole thing. And it's probably the most frustrating thing about this film… I can't show you how good the album is; that's going to be a question for people, but it really is good… I still think all of us involved in the film or the album go back and debate, do we hope it's released? Do we not? Is it better than it isn't released? But I would really like people to be able to hear it because it’s good.

articles.title: Golden Globes: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Goes Comedy, ‘Dune 3’ Skips Box Office Achievement Category and More (EXCLUSIVE)

articles.content:
The Golden Globes ballots are out, and some of the year's biggest surprises are emerging from the official reminder lists sent to members.

Variety has exclusively obtained the official motion picture eligibility list for the 84th Golden Globes, which lays out every film submitted across seven categories along with the actors, directors, writers and composers each studio put forward. The document includes 88 titles for best motion picture (drama), 43 for best motion picture (musical or comedy), 24 animated features, 42 non-English-language films, 100 original scores, 51 original songs and 20 contenders for cinematic and box office achievement. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Hold Onto Me' Director Myrsini Aristidou Kicks Off Historic Oscar Campaign for Sundance Audience Award Winner: 'I Really Feel Like We're Underdogs'

It reveals some unexpected genre placements, ambitious campaign decisions and performers who could find themselves competing against their own work.

There’s the musical or comedy race, which Sony has turned into its own blockbuster lane. “ Spider-Man: Brand New Day ,” which has grossed more than $2 billion worldwide, files on the comedy side of the house with Tom Holland in lead actor. The rest of the ensemble, including Zendaya, Florence Pugh, Mark Ruffalo, Sadie Sink, Marisa Tomei, Jon Bernthal and Tramell Tillman, goes supporting. The studio’s “Jumanji: Open World” follows it in, with Dwayne Johnson, Jack Black and Kevin Hart in lead actor and Karen Gillan in lead actress.

Netflix’s “ The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth ,” directed by David Fincher from a Quentin Tarantino script, joins both the comedy race and the cinematic and box office achievement race, with Brad Pitt in lead actor. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The cinematic and box office achievement category has 20 entries. Introduced in 2024, it recognizes films that have grossed $150 million, with at least $100 million grossed in the U.S., or have garnered “commensurate digital streaming viewership recognized by trusted industry sources.”

One notable omission is Denis Villeneuve’s upcoming sci-fi epic “Dune: Part Three,” which appears in Best Motion Picture (Drama) and Best Original Score but not in the box office race. Of course, its actors, including Timothée Chalamet, are in the mix for acting recognition. Even though the Warner Bros. epic is allowed, based on Globes rules, to use projected grosses, it’s opted out of the category, the same as its predecessor, “Dune: Part Two,” which didn’t submit in the category last time around. “Dune: Part Three” opens Dec. 18. For Netflix, “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” starts a two-week, IMAX-only run Wednesday before it streams Dec. 23, and it’s already on the box office list.

The rest of the box office field includes “Backrooms,” “The Devil Wears Prada 2,” “Disclosure Day,” “Focker In-Law,” “GOAT,” “Godzilla Minus Zero,” “Hoppers,” “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,” “Jumanji: Open World,” “Michael,” “Minions & Monsters,” “Moana,” “Obsession,” “The Odyssey,” “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” “Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu,” “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie,” “Toy Story 5” and A24’s documentary “You Can See Everything,” the only place it can compete on the ballot, likely making it the frontrunner to win the prize.

Animation isn't just found at the kids’ table anymore.

Eight of the 24 animated submissions also turn up in a best picture category. Netflix’s “Ray Gunn,” from two-time Oscar winner Brad Bird, makes a surprise entry in the drama field alongside Leah Nelson’s “Tangles,” Laika’s “Wildwood” from director Travis Knight and Sony Pictures Classics’ “Iron Boy,” which doubles as a French entry in the non-English language field.

The musical or comedy side gets its own animated contingent with DreamWorks Animation’s “Forgotten Island,” Illumination’s “Minions & Monsters” and “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie.” One conspicuous no-show is Pixar’s “Toy Story 5.” The billion-dollar sequel seemed to have skipped the best motion picture (musical or comedy) entirely, competing in animated feature and cinematic and box-office achievement, in addition to Randy Newman’s score and Taylor Swift’s original song “I Knew It, I Knew You.” Interestingly, “Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island,” a Japanese dark fantasy from Toho and director Kei Oikawa, makes the opposite call, appearing in non-English language, score and song but not in animated feature at all. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Several performers will be competing against themselves, and a few could do it in two genres at once. Zendaya has four titles in the running. “Dune: Part Three” and “The Drama” put her in both lead actress races, drama and comedy and “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” put her in supporting. Robert Pattinson also has four, with “Primetime” in drama and “The Drama” in comedy for lead actor, plus “Dune: Part Three” and “The Odyssey” in supporting.

Sandra Hüller makes it a three-way tie at four, with “Rose” in lead actress and “Fatherland,” “Digger” and “Project Hail Mary” in supporting. Anne Hathaway has three: “Verity” in lead actress (drama), “The Devil Wears Prada 2” in lead actress (musical or comedy) and “The Odyssey” in supporting.

Penélope Cruz has three, with “Bunker” in lead actress and “La Bola Negra” and “The Invite” in supporting. Olivia Wilde has three performances, including “I Want Your Sex” and “The Invite” in lead actress (musical or comedy) and “Behemoth!” in supporting. She is also in the running for one of the six slots for best director for “The Invite.”

Brad Pitt is in lead actor twice, for “Heart of the Beast” in drama and “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” in musical or comedy. Andrew Garfield has two, with “The Uprising” in lead actor (drama) and “Artificial” in supporting.
